subject: [PATCH v7 1/6] fuse: decouple fuse_ring creation from ent registration

reviews.author: Bernd Schubert
reviews.summary:
Reviewer argued that introducing a new FUSE_OVER_IO_URING2 flag without announcing its existence in the kernel is not acceptable, as it would introduce a change in behavior without proper notification.

Reviewer expressed concerns about introducing a new flag (FUSE_OVER_IO_URING2) that may break backwards compatibility, citing potential issues with older libfuse versions and existing users relying on the current behavior.
reviews.raw_body:
Well, setting a flag that is not announced by kernel is not ok
either. Yes, it is change in behavior, but it is debatable.

---

I have a basic patch for that, but I fear testing will bring up ore
issues when we switch at run time.

Let's discuss in a few min.


Thanks,
Bernd

2026-08-20.patch_summary: This patch decouples the creation of fuse_ring from entity registration, addressing a potential deadlock issue in flush_bg_queue(). The change aims to improve backwards compatibility by not introducing new flags or breaking existing functionality. Instead, it focuses on fixing the underlying lockdep problem through a more fundamental approach, allowing servers using older versions of libfuse to continue working without issues.

reviews.author: Baokun Li
reviews.summary: Reviewer Baokun Li agreed that decoupling fuse_ring creation from ent registration is a good idea, noting that it structurally eliminates the nesting.
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense \u2014 separating dequeue from send eliminates the nesting
structurally.


Cheers,
Baokun
